title: Total Hom into a bounded injective complex preserves short exact sequences
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, and let $0\to U\xrightarrow{j}V\xrightarrow{p}W\to0$ be a sequence of integer-indexed cochain complexes of $A$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] which is short exact in every degree. Let $I$ be a cochain complex with injective terms [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and let $a\leq b$ be integers such that $I^q=0$ for $q<a$ or $q>b$. Use the $A$-module-valued total Hom complex [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex], with degree-$r$ term $\prod_{s\in\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Hom}_A(M^s,I^{s+r})$ and differential $d_Iz-(-1)^rzd_M$. Componentwise precomposition with $p$ and $j$ defines $A$-linear chain maps $p^*$ and $j^*$, and
$$0\to\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(W,I)\xrightarrow{p^*}\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(V,I)\xrightarrow{j^*}\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(U,I)\to0$$
is short exact in every degree. No support bound on $U,V,W$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0G4H, lemma-finite-ext-into-bounded-injective, proof: bounded injective computation and truncation comparison, expanded at the complex level.

proof.text: Write $H^r(M)=\prod_s\operatorname{Hom}_A(M^s,I^{s+r})$ using [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex]. For a chain map $f:M\to N$ put $(f^*z)_s=z_s f^s$. This is $A$-linear. In component $s$, $d(f^*z)_s=d_I^{s+r}z_sf^s-(-1)^rz_{s+1}f^{s+1}d_M^s=(d_I^{s+r}z_s-(-1)^rz_{s+1}d_N^s)f^s=(f^*dz)_s$, since $f$ commutes with differentials [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Thus $p^*$ and $j^*$ are chain maps, and $j^*p^*=0$ because $p^sj^s=0$ in every degree.

proof.text: Fix $r$. If $p^*z=0$, then $z_sp^s=0$ for each $s$. Surjectivity of $p^s$ gives $z_s(w)=0$ for every $w\in W^s$, by choosing $v\in V^s$ with $p^s(v)=w$. Hence $z=0$ and $p^*:H^r(W)\to H^r(V)$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 0A8H, section-hom-complexes, defining product and signed differential; elementary expansion for the truncation comparison in dualizing.tex Tag 0G4H.

proof.text: If $z\in H^r(V)$ satisfies $j^*z=0$, then $z_s$ vanishes on $\operatorname{im}j^s=\ker p^s$. Define $y_s(w)=z_s(v)$ for any lift $p^s(v)=w$. Two lifts differ by an element of $\ker p^s$, so this is well-defined; lifting sums and scalar multiples shows that $y_s$ is $A$-linear. Therefore $y=(y_s)_s\in H^r(W)$ and $p^*y=z$. Together with Step 1 this proves $\operatorname{im}p^*=\ker j^*$ in degree $r$.

source.place: Tag 0A8H, section-hom-complexes, defining product and signed differential; elementary expansion for the truncation comparison in dualizing.tex Tag 0G4H.

proof.text: For $u=(u_s)_s\in H^r(U)$, injectivity of $I^{s+r}$ in the extension sense stated in [def-sp-injective-resolutions] extends each $u_s:U^s\to I^{s+r}$ across the monomorphism $j^s$ to $v_s:V^s\to I^{s+r}$. Only $a-r\leq s\leq b-r$ have a possibly nonzero target. Choose extensions for this finite set, and take the zero map elsewhere; then $v=(v_s)_s\in H^r(V)$ satisfies $j^*v=u$. These are homogeneous cochains, so no compatibility between the chosen extensions and differentials is required. Thus $j^*$ is surjective in degree $r$. Steps 2--4 give the asserted degreewise short exact sequence, and Step 1 supplies its chain maps. No bound on the source complexes was used.
